steps.title: Inspecting interpreter runtime information with sys

blocks.text: sys.executable identifies the running interpreter’s executable path when available. It may be an empty string or None if Python cannot retrieve it; do not invent a path.
sys.version includes the interpreter version plus build and compiler information.

After import sys, print(sys.executable) and print(sys.version) display the actual executing runtime. Compare these observations with the interpreter you intended, rather than relying only on a tool label.

annotations.text: Observe the actual process, not a tool label.

blocks.text: Use the selected Python executable with -m venv .venv to create a project environment. Its interpreter is bin/python on POSIX or Scripts/python.exe on Windows.
Activation changes command lookup to the environment executable. It is not required when invoking that executable by its full path.
sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix identifies an interpreter running in a virtual environment.
Inspect installed packages using the environment’s Python with -m pip list.
Virtual environments are isolated from base-environment packages by default; do not assume the base package list applies.

public.prompt: POSIX order-report project: /project. Selected base interpreter: /usr/bin/python3. Read each independent transcript and decide whether it proves creation and explicit use of the project venv, a True prefix comparison, and successful package listing.

buckets.label: Does not meet the stated criterion

items.text:
/usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv -> success
/project/.venv/bin/python diagnostic.py
sys.executable: /project/.venv/bin/python
sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix: True
/project/.venv/bin/python -m pip list -> success

/usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv -> success
/usr/bin/python3 diagnostic.py
sys.executable: /usr/bin/python3
sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix: False
/usr/bin/python3 -m pip list -> success

/usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv -> success
/project/.venv/bin/python diagnostic.py
sys.executable: /project/.venv/bin/python
sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix: True
No package listing was performed.

excerpt1.message: Creation, explicit venv execution, prefix comparison and listing all meet the criterion.

excerpt2.message: The later commands use system Python, not the created environment.

excerpt3.message: The required package-listing evidence is missing.

blocks.text: Inspect sys.executable in the executed program to identify its actual interpreter. An environment label is not the evidence for this check.
A venv interpreter is at bin/python on POSIX or Scripts/python.exe on Windows.
If command lookup selects the wrong Python, configure the tool to invoke the intended venv executable explicitly. Explicit invocation does not require activation.
After changing the runtime, check the executable path and sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix again in the program that runs. Changing the displayed label is not the final check.

public.prompt: Read each editor-change and rerun excerpt. On POSIX the intended existing interpreter is /project/.venv/bin/python. Decide whether the change is verified by the actual rerun.

buckets.label: Does not meet the stated criterion

items.text:
Editor executable = /project/.venv/bin/python
Rerun sys.executable = /project/.venv/bin/python
Rerun sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix = True

Editor label = .venv
Rerun sys.executable = /usr/bin/python3
Rerun sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix = False

Editor executable = /project/.venv/bin/python
No rerun has occurred.

excerpt1.message: The explicit selection and both rerun observations identify the intended venv.

excerpt2.message: The label does not override the system-runtime evidence.

excerpt3.message: The selected executable has not been verified in a new process.
